episodes.title: Sangam's Five Landscapes
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part I, Class XII, Themes 2-3 (reprint 2020-21), https://archive.org/details/ncert-lehs1 (read 2026-11-16)

Wikipedia, "Sangam landscape", citing S. Balambal, Studies in the History of the Sangam Age (1998), pp. 27-28, and U. Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008), table 7.3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangam_landscape (read 2026-11-16)

Wikipedia, "Sangam literature", citing K. Zvelebil, Tamil Literature (1974), pp. 9-11, and T. Takahashi, Tamil Love Poetry and Poetics (1995), pp. 3-5, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangam_literature (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: In Sangam poetry, which landscape goes with lovers waiting patiently?
quiz.why: Mullai, the forest and pasture, is the landscape of patient waiting.

quiz.q: What does 'akam' poetry deal with?
quiz.why: Akam is the inner world of love; puram is war and public life.

quiz.q: What does the word 'tinai' mean here?
quiz.why: Tinai is the landscape a poem is set in, each tied to a mood.

episodes.title: The Nine Rasas
sources: The Natyasastra, ascribed to Bharata-Muni, Vol. I, tr. Manomohan Ghosh (Calcutta: Royal Asiatic Society of Bengal, 1950), ch. VI, vv. 15-17, 31-43 and note to v. 15, pp. 102-108, https://archive.org/details/dli.csl.6367 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Why does the Natyashastra call it 'rasa'?
options: Because it is written in verse
quiz.why: The text says rasa is so called because it is capable of being tasted.

quiz.q: Which rasa was added later by writers on poetics?
quiz.why: The Natyashastra has eight rasas; later writers added shanta, peace.

quiz.q: According to Bharata, which rasa grows out of the erotic (shringara)?
quiz.why: A mimicry of the erotic is called the comic, hasya.

episodes.title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
sources: The Panchatantra, translated from the Sanskrit by Arthur W. Ryder (University of Chicago Press, 1925), Introduction pp. 13-15 and Book IV "Loss of Gains", "The Monkey and the Crocodile", pp. 381-388; archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.37110 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Why did the crocodile take the monkey out to sea?
options: Because his wife wanted the monkey's heart
quiz.why: His wife reasoned that a heart fed on such sweet fruit must be like nectar, and asked for it.

quiz.q: Which quality does the monkey show, in GS4 terms?
quiz.why: In deep water he did not panic or plead; he thought of a way back to land.

quiz.q: In the Panchatantra's frame story, who teaches the princes?
quiz.why: Vishnusharman, an eighty-year-old teacher, promised to teach them in six months.

episodes.title: Paintings Behind Fallen Walls
sources: Neel Rekha, "Maithil Paintings: An Enquiry into Its Historiographical Trajectory (1947-1997)", Folkartopedia, https://www.folkartopedia.com/folk-painting/maithil-paintings-an-enquiry-into-its-historiographical-trajectory-sk/ (read 2026-11-16)
"Madhubani Painting: A Historical Context", Folkartopedia (1 April 2020), https://www.folkartopedia.com/archive/madhubani-painting-a-historical-context-sk/ (read 2026-11-16)
W. G. Archer, "Maithil Painting", Marg, Vol. 3, No. 3 (1949), pp. 24-33 (as cited)

Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, Registration details of Geographical Indications (2007-08 list: No. 31, application 37, Madhubani Paintings, Bihar), https://www.ipindia.gov.in/storage/uploads/docs-operator/aa9ef4c8-ae0e-4717-9181-52b6a9479b82.pdf (read 2026-11-16)
NCERT, An Introduction to Indian Art, Part I, Class XI, ch. 5

quiz.q: How did an outsider first come to notice Mithila wall paintings in 1934?
options: On walls exposed by an earthquake
In a printed book of folk tales
quiz.why: Inspecting damage after the January 1934 earthquake, W. G. Archer saw paintings on the newly exposed inner walls.

quiz.q: What helped Madhubani painting travel beyond Mithila?
options: Painting on paper, during the 1966-68 drought
A royal order of the Darbhanga court
quiz.why: During the drought, women were encouraged to paint on paper, which could be carried and sold.

quiz.q: Madhubani painting is a registered Geographical Indication of which state?
quiz.why: "Madhubani Paintings" is registered as a GI of Bihar (2007-08 list).

episodes.title: The Constitution Before the Constitution
sources: A. Berriedale Keith, A Constitutional History of India 1600-1935 (London: Methuen, 1936), pp. 70-77, 95-99, 131-135, 165-167, 229-231, 245-249, 322-440; https://archive.org/details/constitutionalhi00berr (read 2026-11-16)
NCERT, Indian Constitution at Work, Class XI, ch. 1 'Constitution: Why and How?'; https://archive.org/details/ncert-keps2 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, what could the Governor-General not do?
quiz.why: He had no power to override his council; he had only a casting vote on a tie.

quiz.q: Which Act brought dyarchy to the provinces?
quiz.why: The Montagu-Chelmsford Act of 1919 split provincial subjects into transferred and reserved.

quiz.q: Who elected the members of the Constituent Assembly?
options: Provincial assemblies set up under the 1935 Act
quiz.why: NCERT: members were chosen by indirect election by the provincial assemblies of the 1935 Act.

episodes.title: The Drain of Wealth in Six Cards
sources: Dadabhai Naoroji, Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (London: Swan Sonnenschein, 1901), Introduction pp. v-viii, pp. 24-25, 33, 38, 56-57, https://archive.org/details/cu31924022963916 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: What did Naoroji call the 'moral drain'?
options: Experience taken to England by retiring officials
quiz.why: Top posts went to Europeans who took their experience home: a loss of wealth, wisdom and work.

quiz.q: Why did Naoroji call the rule 'un-British'?
options: It was run by the French
It went against Britain's own ideals
It was paid for by Britain
quiz.why: He held the rulers to their own ideals: despotic to Indians, suicidal to Britain.

quiz.q: In which year was 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' published?
quiz.why: The book appeared in 1901, collecting his earlier papers.

episodes.title: Three Ways to Tax a Field
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part III, Class XII, Theme 10 "Colonialism and the Countryside" (reprint 2019-20), https://archive.org/details/ncert-lehs3 (read 2026-11-16)
NCERT, Our Pasts III, Class VIII, ch. 3 "Ruling the Countryside" (reprint 2020-21), pp. 27-29, https://archive.org/details/ncert-hess2 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: What happened at the Burdwan auction of 1797?
options: Most buyers were the raja's own servants and agents
The auction was cancelled by rain
quiz.why: Over 95 per cent of the sale was fictitious; the raja stayed in control.

quiz.q: Under the mahalwari system, who collected the revenue?
quiz.why: Revenue was fixed per village (mahal) and collected by the headman.

quiz.q: In which year was the Permanent Settlement introduced in Bengal?
quiz.why: It came into operation in 1793; mahalwari came in 1822.

episodes.title: The Play That Shook the Indigo Planters
sources: NCERT, Our Pasts III, Class VIII, ch. 2, "The 'Blue Rebellion' and After" (reprint 2020-21), quoting the Indigo Commission Report (1860), Vol. II, Minutes of Evidence, p. 67
Dinabandhu Mitra, Nil Darpan, or the Indigo Planting Mirror, translated from the Bengali by a Native (Calcutta: C. H. Manuel, 1861), Introduction and Author's Preface; Project Gutenberg #54027
Nurul Hossain Choudhury, "Long, Rev. James", Banglapedia, https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Long,_Rev._James (read 2026-11-16)
Wikipedia, "Nil Darpan" (read 2026-11-16), citing G. A. Oddie, Missionaries, Rebellion and Proto-Nationalism (Routledge, 1999)

quiz.q: Why was the missionary James Long tried in 1861?
options: For having the English Nil Darpan printed
For refusing to pay indigo rent
For writing the Indigo Commission report
quiz.why: Planters prosecuted him for libel over the translation he had printed; he was fined one thousand rupees and jailed for a month.

quiz.q: What does Nil Darpan show about literature in the national story?
options: It carried peasants' grievances to the educated public
It was written to praise the planters
quiz.why: The drama put the ryots' story before readers in Calcutta and beyond, and its trial made it widely known.

quiz.q: When did thousands of ryots in Bengal refuse to grow indigo?
quiz.why: NCERT dates the 'Blue Rebellion' to March 1859.

episodes.title: 1857 in Eight Places
sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History Part III (Class XII), Theme 11 'Rebels and the Raj', pp. 288-289, §1.3 and chapter timeline (reprint 2019-20), https://archive.org/details/ncert-lehs3 (read 2026-11-16)
Surendra Nath Sen, Eighteen Fifty-Seven (Publications Division, Government of India, 1957), chs. 2, 4-8, 10, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.43239 (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Where did the revolt of 1857 begin, on 10 May?
quiz.why: The sepoys of the Meerut cantonment rose on 10 May; Delhi followed on 11 May.

quiz.q: How did the revolt spread, according to NCERT?
options: All towns rose on the same day
It began in Bihar and moved west
As news reached each town, its sepoys rose
quiz.why: Placed in date order, the mutinies show news travelling from one town to the next.

quiz.q: Who led the rebels at Arrah in Bihar?
quiz.why: Kunwar Singh, a zamindar of Arrah, led the rising there; Arrah rose on 27 July 1857.

episodes.title: Rammohun Roy's Argument
sources: NCERT, Our Pasts III, Class VIII, ch. 8 "Women, Caste and Reform" (reprint 2020-21)
Jogendra Chunder Ghose (ed.), The English Works of Raja Rammohun Roy, Vol. I (Calcutta, 1901), Introduction pp. xviii-xix; archive.org theenglishworks01rammuoft
Bengal Regulation XVII of 1829 (dated as in Ghose, 4 December 1829)

quiz.q: How did Rammohun Roy mainly argue against sati?
options: By leading protests in the street
By showing it had no sanction in the ancient texts
By asking Parliament to rule India directly
By founding a newspaper in London
quiz.why: He read the texts closely and argued in pamphlets, often written as dialogues, that the practice had no sanction in them.

quiz.q: Which method did later reformers borrow from him?
options: Quoting early texts against a present practice
quiz.why: NCERT notes later reformers, like Vidyasagar, used the same strategy of citing ancient texts.

quiz.q: In which year was sati banned by regulation in Bengal?
quiz.why: Regulation XVII of 1829, dated 4 December 1829.
